To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed methodology can be employed for the classification of L8 data into 27 land cover classes with high accuracy rates; (ii) SVMs are more accurate and computationally efficient than CNNs; (iii) employing images with up to ~30% cloud cover is more accurate than employing images with lower cloud cover; and (iv) employing all images is slightly more accurate than employing the top-ranked images.

(i) the proposed methodology for detailed land cover mapping from L8 data is capable to produce high-quality land cover maps with overall accuracy rates of more than 90%; (ii) the proposed methodology is robust to different cloud cover percentages and can be employed with up to 70% cloud cover; and (iii) the shallow SVM framework was able to outperform the patch-based CNN framework in terms of accuracy, while the CNN framework was able to achieve higher per-class accuracy rates for most classes

(a) the proposed methodology is capable of generating detailed land cover maps with high accuracy rates, and (b) the SVM framework outperformed the patch-based deep CNN framework in all experiments, but the latter is more suitable for large-scale applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the classification of annual satellite imagery with high cloud cover and the development of an appropriate nomenclature.
the development of a detailed and accurate classification methodology for high-resolution satellite data and the investigation of cloud cover influence on classification accuracy.
the development of a detailed and accurate land cover map based on a large set of L8 images and the evaluation of different cloud cover scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given dataset, the most appropriate cloud cover percentage and the most suitable classification framework should be selected in a data-driven fashion.
the presented methodology is able to deliver accurate land cover maps with a relatively low cloud cover percentage and a high degree of detail.
the proposed methodology is capable of delivering accurate and detailed land cover maps from high-resolution satellite data even when a considerable amount of cloud cover is present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in general, SVMs are more robust to cloud contamination than deep CNNs, but the latter is more flexible and accurate in the case of cloud-free data.
a detailed land cover classification can be achieved by using a relatively small amount of cloud-covered data and by employing a shallow kernel-based classification framework.
the presented methodology can deliver accurate land cover maps at a relatively low computational expense and with minimal data preparation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cloud cover can be effectively addressed in a multitemporal classification approach, which is a key requirement for detailed land cover mapping.
the application of multitemporal satellite data with up to 20–30% cloud cover is feasible for detailed land cover mapping.
the presented methodology is able to produce accurate and detailed land cover maps from multitemporal L8 data with up to 70% cloud cover.
